head: ce44ce8a1f1c9c01bef1ef06776a37a7ac09f1a1
summary: Four added Scaladoc entries contradict edge cases implemented by the runtime helpers.  |  Several added docs omit or misstate edge-case behavior of the runtime implementations.  |  The added Scaladoc is accurately placed and matches the implementations; only redundant return tags need minor cleanup.  |  Two added comments overstate behavior that the compiler/runtime implementation does not provide.  |  All 37 added Scaladoc groups accurately match their primitive signatures and boxing bridge implementations; the diff is comment-only.  |  The bridge-method documentation omits its observable null and type-mismatch behavior; the diff is otherwise comment-only.

items.issue: The documented exception condition is incomplete for the explicitly permitted unvalidated constructor bounds. For example, `new ArrayCharSequence(xs, -1, 1).charAt(0)` passes the documented `index` range check but then throws from `xs(-1)`.
items.suggestion: State that an in-range sequence index can still throw `ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException` when the sequence was constructed with invalid underlying-array bounds, or validate those bounds in the constructor (outside this comment-only PR).

items.issue: The claim that invalid bounds yield the sequence's in-range characters is false for a negative `start`: `start` is clamped to zero but `length` remains `end - this.start`. With `start = -2` and `end = 5`, it copies seven characters starting at zero, rather than the intersection of the declared slice with the array.
items.suggestion: Describe the actual clamping calculation, or correct the implementation if intersecting the declared slice was intended.

items.issue: `NullValue` is not a control state only while a lazy val is unbound. The compiler stores it after a lazy val has successfully evaluated to `null`, as the persistent sentinel for that computed value.
items.suggestion: Describe `Evaluating` and `Waiting` as evaluation control states, and `NullValue` as the sentinel representing an initialized lazy val whose value is `null`.

items.issue: The class documentation promises that resolved module instances are cached per class, but `ModuleSerializationProxy.instances` uses `ClassValueCompat`, whose fallback calls `computeValue` on every access when `java.lang.ClassValue` is unavailable.
items.suggestion: Qualify the cache claim: resolution is cached per class when `java.lang.ClassValue` is available; the compatibility fallback does not cache.

items.issue: The summary says it tests for at least `atLevel` dimensions, but `atLevel <= 0` returns `false` for every array: `isArrayClass` only stops successfully at exactly level 1.
items.suggestion: Document the non-positive-level behavior, or limit the dimensionality claim explicitly to positive `atLevel` values without implying an unenforced constraint.

items.issue: The zero-step `@throws` is incomplete. The returned `NumericRange` also throws `IllegalArgumentException` when its lazily computed length exceeds `Int.MaxValue`; the default-step overload has the same deferred failure.
items.suggestion: State that computing the range length can throw `IllegalArgumentException` for a zero step or for a range with more than `Int.MaxValue` elements, and add the corresponding case to the default-step overload's documentation.

items.issue: The zero-step `@throws` omits the other deferred `NumericRange.length` failure: an `IllegalArgumentException` when the range has more than `Int.MaxValue` elements. The default-step overload omits it too.
items.suggestion: Document both deferred `IllegalArgumentException` conditions for both `to` overloads.

items.issue: `maxElements` is documented as an upper bound, but negative values are accepted and cause `take(maxElements)` to render zero elements; zero is not “at most” a negative bound.
items.suggestion: Document that a negative `maxElements` renders no collection or array elements, or otherwise phrase the bound only for non-negative values while stating the negative case.

items.issue: The documentation omits that, after the cache becomes megamorphic, delegated `MegaMethodCache.find` calls `Class.getMethod` and can throw `NoSuchMethodException` instead of returning `null`.
items.suggestion: Add an `@throws NoSuchMethodException` tag for a megamorphic lookup whose receiver class lacks the required public method.

items.issue: It says every call records `m` and replaces the cache with an extended cache. A `MegaMethodCache.add` returns itself and deliberately records no per-receiver entry, so neither claim holds once the site is megamorphic.
items.suggestion: Describe the operation as replacing the soft reference with `get.add(receiver, m)` and note that a megamorphic cache remains unchanged while `m` is still returned.

items.issue: The `@return` tag repeats the complete `Returns ...` summary without adding an edge case or other information.
The `@return` tag repeats the complete `Returns ...` summary without adding information.
The `@return` tag restates the return value already fully described by the opening `Creates ...` summary and delegation explanation.
The `@return` tag is a direct repetition of the opening `Returns ...` sentence; the same redundant-tag pattern recurs in the added factory and extractor documentation.
items.suggestion: Remove return tags that add no information beyond their `Returns ...` summaries.

items.issue: The `@return` tag repeats the complete opening summary. The same boilerplate is repeated for every fixed-arity and XXL tupled-function witness.
items.suggestion: Remove these redundant `@return` tags from the tupled-function family.

items.issue: The comment says the compiler calls this when optimizing `Tuple.toArray` on tuples statically known to have at most 22 elements. The optimizer handles the statically known empty tuple separately with `Array.emptyObjectArray`; it calls `productToArray` only for arities 1 through 22.
items.suggestion: Say that the compiler calls it for statically known non-empty tuples of arity at most 22, or remove the optimizer-detail sentence.

items.issue: The summary promises only elements added to the builder, but every factory returns an `ArraySeq` over its full length-`n` array and tracks no final count. Calling `result()` early exposes unfilled default values; adding too many elements fails only through array indexing. The repeated `@param n` claims that exactly `n` elements will be added, but this is not enforced.
items.suggestion: Document `n` as the storage capacity and qualify the result guarantee on compiler-generated callers adding exactly `n` elements, or add bookkeeping/validation that enforces the stated contract.

items.issue: This `apply` bridge (and every corresponding bridge in this chunk) documents unboxing but omits material behavior of the `Any` arguments: `BoxesRunTime.unboxToInt(null)` supplies `0` (and the analogous helpers supply `0L`/`0.0d`), while a non-null value of the wrong boxed type throws `ClassCastException`.
items.suggestion: Document the null-to-zero conversion and add an `@throws ClassCastException` for non-null arguments that are not the matching boxed primitive type, consistently on all bridge `apply` methods.
